summary: Server game-state component that drives loading a session (new game or savegame) through esv::SessionLoadSystem::Update (game bg3.exe+0x2B1D4B0, Toolkit EoCServer.dll+0xC49A20): starts with an eoc::LoadSessionDesc (load target description: ids, module Guids, ruleset modifiers), then the savegame visitor, a string and the step counter of the load state machine (0..8: StartLoadSession, SetupLoadGame, LoadGlobalsPart1/2/3, LoadStory, finish). Read as a condition by many server systems (photo mode, drop-in, icons, rulesets, dialog privacy). Never seen alive. Registry total 176 (server row); the Toolkit build has 0xA0 (its LoadSessionDesc is 0x10 shorter).

fields.name: Value
fields.evidence: Toolkit eoc::LoadSessionDesc::Visit visits +0x20 as HashMap<ls::Guid, ls::Variant<eoc::ruleset::NoneValue,int,float,ls::FixedString,bool>>; this Variant is 8 bytes with the value at +0 and the alternative index at +4 (Toolkit EoCShared.dll+0x18EAA0, same Variant).

fields.name: Type
fields.evidence: Variant alternative index: 0 none, 1 int, 2 float, 3 FixedString, 4 bool.

fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: Desc constructor bg3.exe+0xF19960 (called by creator bg3.exe+0x300C460): `p[0] = 0`. Toolkit eoc::LoadSessionDesc move ctor (EoCShared.dll+0x121F640) copies 4 bytes at +0; Visit sends it first as uint.

fields.name: field_4
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0xF19960: `p[1] = 0xFFFFFFFF`; desc destructor bg3.exe+0x5F1BB0 DecRefs +4. Toolkit: FixedString at +4, visited.

fields.name: field_8
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0xF19960 stores an IncRef'ed default FixedString (DAT_14617662c); destructor DecRefs +8. Toolkit Visit sends it with VisitGUID (a Guid kept as FixedString).

fields.name: _PadC
fields.evidence: alignment of the Array at +0x10; not written by the constructor.

fields.name: Guids
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0xF19960 zeroes +0x10/+0x18; destructor frees +0x10 (FUN_1405BD630, trivial elements). Toolkit Visit: size at +0x1C, elements `+0x10` with stride 0x10 visited as Guid (module/target Guids).

fields.name: RulesetModifiers
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0xF19960 builds +0x20 with FUN_140F19B50; destructor bg3.exe+0x5F1BB0 frees +0x50 and the hash parts from +0x20 (64 bytes up to +0x60). Toolkit Visit: `ruleset::Visit((HashMap<Guid, Variant<NoneValue,int,float,FixedString,bool>>*)(this + 0x20))`.

fields.name: field_60
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0xF19960: IncRef'ed default FixedString at +0x60; destructor DecRefs +0x60. Toolkit: FixedString at +0x60 visited with VisitGUID.

fields.name: _Pad64
fields.evidence: alignment; not written by the constructor.

fields.name: field_68
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0xF19960 zeroes the qword at +0x68; trivially destroyed. Not in the Toolkit's (older) LoadSessionDesc.

fields.name: field_80
fields.evidence: Creator zeroes +0x80. Update bg3.exe+0x2B1D4B0 line 474: `*(uint32*)(*(p + 0x80) + 0xA0) = 1` in the final step - a pointer to some load object.

fields.name: SavegameVisitor
fields.evidence: Creator zeroes +0x88. esv::SessionLoadSystem::SetupLoadGame (bg3.exe+0x2B1DEA0) stores `*(p + 0x88) = FUN_142A3B030(savegameManager, 0)`; the update passes it as `SavegameVisitor*` to LoadGlobalsPart1/2 (bg3.exe+0x2B1E3F0) and frees it in step 8 (`FUN_141113310(*(p+0x88), 1); *(p+0x88) = 0`). Toolkit: the same visitor at +0x70.

fields.name: field_90
fields.evidence: Creator constructs an STDString at +0x90 from a global empty string; component destructor bg3.exe+0x22CDCB0 frees it when capacity (+0xA4) > 15 and resets size +0xA0 / capacity 0xF.

fields.name: State
fields.evidence: Creator writes 0 at +0xA8. Update bg3.exe+0x2B1D4B0: `switch(*(uint32*)(p + 0xA8))` with cases 0..8 and writes 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 as the load proceeds; Toolkit the same at +0x98.

open_questions: Names of the desc members at +0, +4, +8, +0x60 are unknown (eoc::LoadSessionDesc has no member names in the Toolkit); +8 and +0x60 hold Guids as FixedStrings.
+0x68..+0x7F (three zeroed qwords, part of the game's longer LoadSessionDesc) and +0x80 are not explained.
The HashMap value stride (8) comes from the Toolkit's Variant, not from game code read here.
Not seen alive (seen.py has no samples).
